name: You're Dead!
editorial_article: Released in 2014 via Warp Records, "You're Dead!" is the fifth studio album by the visionary Los Angeles-based producer Flying Lotus (Steven Ellison). A sprawling and intensely focused concept album, the work serves as a meditation on death and the afterlife, aiming to capture the essence of what comes next rather than serving as a morbid eulogy. Recorded primarily at Ellison’s home studio, the album highlights his mastery of blending modern electronic production with the improvisational freedom of jazz fusion. Key to the album’s distinct, kinetic sound is the ongoing collaboration with bassist Thundercat, who contributes virtuosic performances across almost every track, grounding the frantic, polyrhythmic electronic soundscapes in earthy, liquid basslines.\n\nThe album features a wide range of contributors, including Kendrick Lamar, Kamasi Washington, Snoop Dogg, and Herbie Hancock, reflecting the deep, interconnected web of the contemporary Los Angeles jazz and hip-hop scenes. Sonically, it is noted for its high dynamic range and complex structures, characterized by syncopated rhythms and dense, multi-layered textures. The cover art, a surreal and disturbing masterpiece created by manga artist Shintaro Kago, sets the tone for the album’s blend of the gruesome and the transcendent. "You're Dead!" is widely considered a landmark in 2010s experimental music, successfully bridging the gap between underground beat music and traditional jazz experimentation while securing its place as one of the most intellectually ambitious projects in Flying Lotus’s extensive discography.
